headline: Over 100 Deaths In Himachal Pradesh In Rail-Related Incidents This Monsoon
content: A total of 101 people have died in rain-related incidents in Himachal Pradesh since the onset of monsoon on June 30, the government said on Wednesday. The rain-related incidents include flash floods, landslides, drowning, snake bites, electrocution and falling from height. According to the data shared by the State Emergency Operations Centre, 16, the most, deaths were reported from Kangra district. Fourteen each died in Lahaul and Spiti and Sirmaur, 13 each in Chamba and Shimla, 10 in Mandi, nine in Kullu, three each in Una, Kinnaur and Hamirpur, two in Bilaspur and one in Solan district in rain accidents. The centre pegged the state loss to rain at Rs 1,176 crore. Since Tuesday, Naina Devi received 86.4 mm of rainfall, Olinda 69.4 mm, Kangra 45.8 mm, Amb 38.8 mm, Nangal Dam 38.4 mm, Nalagarh 35 mm, Dharamshala 27.3 mm, Jogindernagar 26 mm and Dhaulakuan 25.5 mm. Thunderstorms and lightning lashed Sundernagar, Shimla, Kangra, Murari Devi and Jubberhatti. The Shimla Met office on Wednesday issued a yellow warning of heavy rain in isolated areas of the state on September 1. Eighty-two roads were closed for vehicular traffic in the state as on Wednesday evening, while 13 water supply schemes and five power transformers were scuppered. Thirty-seven roads were closed in Mandi, 20 in Kullu, seven in Kangra, five each in Chamba and Sirmaur, four in Una, three in Shimla, and one in Lahaul and Spiti district. Between August 1 and August 26, the state received 198.1 mm of rainfall against a normal of 227.2 mm, a deficit of 13 per cent.
